findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() contains dead/confusing logic that always returns false
findings.body: The helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then has `if enabled { return false }` followed by an unconditional `return false`. Both branches return false, so the function always disables SQL expressions regardless of the `FlagSqlExpressions` toggle state. While the intended effect (permanently disabling the vulnerable feature) matches the goal of this security PR, the code reads as though the feature flag controls the outcome when it actually has no effect at all. There is no comment explaining this is a deliberate kill-switch for CVE-2024-9264. A future maintainer could easily 'simplify' this apparent dead code (e.g. by returning `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` directly) and unknowingly re-enable the vulnerable SQL expression code path, since nothing in the code documents why it must always be false.

findings.title: Misleading error message for a feature that is deliberately disabled, not unimplemented
findings.body: When a SQL expression query is submitted, `ReadQuery` now returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". This is inaccurate: the feature was previously implemented and working, and is being force-disabled here as an emergency security mitigation (CVE-2024-9264), not because it was never built. Users/admins who had the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle enabled before upgrading will see a confusing message that doesn't reflect the real reason the feature stopped working, making it harder to diagnose the regression after upgrade.

findings.title: No tests added or updated to verify the SQL-expressions disablement, likely breaking existing coverage
findings.body: This PR replaces the DuckDB-backed `DB` implementation with a stub whose `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` methods unconditionally return `errors.New("not implemented")`, and pairs it with a reader.go change that unconditionally rejects QueryTypeSQL. No test files are included in the diff, yet pkg/expr/sql/parser.go (table extraction via DuckDB AST parsing) and pkg/expr/sql_command.go (SQL command execution) are exactly the kind of logic that would normally have unit tests asserting successful parsing/execution against a real DuckDB instance. Those pre-existing tests, if they exist, would now fail since every call into the stub returns an error instead of real results, and this PR does not update or remove them. Additionally, for a PR whose explicit purpose is to close an RCE/LFI vulnerability, there is no new regression test asserting that `ReadQuery` rejects SQL expression queries regardless of the `FlagSqlExpressions` toggle state, or that the stub DB always errors. Without such tests, there is no CI safety net to catch an accidental future re-enablement of the vulnerable path.
